subject: Gripes about layer_ribbons: no alpha, had to use arrange()

messages.author: c1cb392dfeeacea0
messages.subject: Gripes about layer_ribbons: no alpha, had to use arrange()
parts:
Apparently there's no alpha support in layer_ribbons at all right now. Also, it's annoying that I have to use arrange() for ribbons. I think ribbons (unlike areas) should auto-arrange by x, like its ggplot2 counterpart does, and just like lines in ggvis.

For example, to get the [near] equivalent of 

ggplot(my.df, aes(x=my.x)) + geom_ribbon(mapping=aes(ymin= my.y.min, ymax= my.y.max, fill=factor(my.factor)), alpha=.15) 

I had to

my.df %>% group_by(my.factor) %>% arrange(my.x) %>% ggvis(x= ~my.x, y = ~my.y.min, y2 = ~my.y.max, fill = ~my.factor, alpha := .15) %>% layer_ribbons()

Except of course the alpha part doesn't work at all so if the regions overlap the ggvis output is more confusing than what I get from ggplot.

And without the post-group arrange by x I get gobbledygook.

messages.subject: Re: Gripes about layer_ribbons: no alpha, had to use arrange()
parts: Ah, never mind about the "alpha" part, I discovered I should use "opacity" instead and that works fine. This info might be worth adding to the "Conversion from ggplot2" section in the documentation.
